## Proof

We characterize the topology on $\wp(Y)$ as the **Vietoris topology** (also called the *finite topology* or the *hit-or-miss topology*). We describe its sub-basis and prove that a set-valued map $\varphi: X \to \wp(Y)$ is continuous (with respect to this topology) if and only if it is both upper and lower semicontinuous.

### Definitions

Recall the two standard semicontinuity notions for a set-valued map $\varphi: X \to \wp(Y)$:

- **Upper semicontinuous (usc):** For every open set $V \subseteq Y$, the **upper preimage**
$$\varphi^{+}(V) \;=\; \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \subseteq V \,\}$$
is open in $X$.

- **Lower semicontinuous (lsc):** For every open set $V \subseteq Y$, the **lower preimage**
$$\varphi^{-}(V) \;=\; \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \cap V \neq \emptyset \,\}$$
is open in $X$.

### The topology on $\wp(Y)$

Define a topology $\tau_V$ on $\wp(Y)$ generated by the following sub-basis $\mathcal{S}$:

$$\mathcal{S} \;=\; \big\{\, [V] : V \subseteq Y \text{ open}\,\big\} \;\cup\; \big\{\, \langle V \rangle : V \subseteq Y \text{ open}\,\big\},$$

where:
- $[V] \;=\; \{\, A \in \wp(Y) : A \subseteq V \,\}$ — the collection of all subsets of $Y$ **contained in** $V$ (the *miss* part: $A$ misses $Y \setminus V$),
- $\langle V \rangle \;=\; \{\, A \in \wp(Y) : A \cap V \neq \emptyset \,\}$ — the collection of all subsets of $Y$ that **hit** $V$.

This is the **Vietoris topology** on $\wp(Y)$.

### The equivalence

We now prove:

> $\varphi: X \to \wp(Y)$ is continuous (with $\wp(Y)$ carrying $\tau_V$) $\iff$ $\varphi$ is both upper and lower semicontinuous.

**($\Rightarrow$) Continuity implies both usc and lsc.**

Suppose $\varphi$ is continuous. Then the preimage of every sub-basis element is open in $X$ (since continuity is determined by sub-basis elements).

- For any open $V \subseteq Y$, the set $[V] \in \mathcal{S}$ is open in $\wp(Y)$, so
$$\varphi^{-1}([V]) = \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \in [V] \,\} = \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \subseteq V \,\} = \varphi^{+}(V)$$
is open in $X$. Hence $\varphi$ is upper semicontinuous.

- For any open $V \subseteq Y$, the set $\langle V \rangle \in \mathcal{S}$ is open in $\wp(Y)$, so
$$\varphi^{-1}(\langle V \rangle) = \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \in \langle V \rangle \,\} = \{\, x \in X : \varphi(x) \cap V \neq \emptyset \,\} = \varphi^{-}(V)$$
is open in $X$. Hence $\varphi$ is lower semicontinuous.

**($\Leftarrow$) Both usc and lsc imply continuity.**

Suppose $\varphi$ is both upper and lower semicontinuous. To show $\varphi$ is continuous, it suffices to show that the preimage of every sub-basis element is open (a map is continuous iff the preimage of every sub-basis element is open).

- For any $[V] \in \mathcal{S}$: $\varphi^{-1}([V]) = \varphi^{+}(V)$, which is open by upper semicontinuity.
- For any $\langle V \rangle \in \mathcal{S}$: $\varphi^{-1}(\langle V \rangle) = \varphi^{-}(V)$, which is open by lower semicontinuity.

Since the preimage of every sub-basis element is open, $\varphi$ is continuous. $\square$

### Summary / Characterization

The desired topology on $\wp(Y)$ is the **Vietoris topology**, whose sub-basis is:

$$\boxed{\mathcal{S} \;=\; \{\,[V] : V \subseteq Y \text{ open}\,\} \;\cup\; \{\,\langle V \rangle : V \subseteq Y \text{ open}\,\},}$$

where $[V] = \{A \subseteq Y : A \subseteq V\}$ (the "contained in" or "miss" sets) and $\langle V \rangle = \{A \subseteq Y : A \cap V \neq \emptyset\}$ (the "hit" sets).

The two halves of the sub-basis correspond exactly to the two semicontinuity conditions:
- The **upper Vietoris topology** (generated by $\{[V]\}$) governs upper semicontinuity via $\varphi^{+}(V) = \varphi^{-1}([V])$.
- The **lower Vietoris topology** (generated by $\{\langle V \rangle\}$) governs lower semicontinuity via $\varphi^{-}(V) = \varphi^{-1}(\langle V \rangle)$.

The full Vietoris topology is the join (coarsest common refinement) of these two, and continuity with respect to it is precisely the conjunction of upper and lower semicontinuity.
